narrative: Someone used my card number at gas stations in another state on September 2, 11 transactions of $75 each. I still have my card. I reported it on September 3 and the Bank froze the card but only credited back 6 of the 11 charges. The rep said the other 5 are under investigation. That is $375 of my money.

I was charged a $35 NSF fee for a payment that was RETURNED. So the bank didn't even pay it and still charged me. Then the gym tried again the next day and I got another $35. $70 in fees for a $40 gym membership that never went through.

I requested a payoff quote on my personal loan on August 28 and was told $6,214.50 good through September 5. I sent exactly that on September 2. Now I got a statement saying I still owe $187.33 and the loan is still showing open. Nobody can tell me where that number came from.

Got a collection notice for $1,488 from a company I never heard of saying they bought my old Bank checking account debt. I asked them for validation by certified mail on August 15. Instead of sending it they sent another notice for a higher amount, $1,560.

I pay my car loan on the Bank's website on the 15th every month. In August the website took the payment, gave me a confirmation number, and the money left my account. Then on September 1 I get a call saying I'm 17 days late. They found the payment sitting in suspense and applied it, but the late mark is still on my credit.

I am writing this letter because I have called the Bank more times than I can count and I am out of options, so please read the whole thing even though it is long. My husband and I have had our mortgage with the Bank since 2015 and we were never late, not one time, until this year. In February my husband had emergency back surgery and he was out of work for almost four months. He drives a delivery route and could not lift anything. I work part time in a school cafeteria and my paycheck does not cover the mortgage by itself. On April 3 I called the Bank and asked for help. The woman I spoke to was very kind and she set us up with a forbearance for three months, April, May and June. She explained that at the end we would need to work out how to pay back the missed payments and that there were different options. I wrote down her name and the reference number. We got a letter on April 10 confirming the forbearance. In June my husband went back to work, thank God, but only part time at first. On July 2 I called to ask about the options for the missed payments, which come to $5,961. I was told the options were to pay it all at once, do a repayment plan where we would pay an extra $993 a month for six months, or apply for a loan modification. We could not do the lump sum or the extra $993, so I asked for the modification application. It took two weeks to get it in the mail. I filled it out and sent it with all our pay stubs, bank statements, tax returns and the hardship letter from my husband's doctor on July 21 by certified mail. On August 4 I got a letter saying the application was incomplete because the tax return was missing. It was not missing, I have a copy of everything I sent and the certified mail receipt. I sent the tax return again. On August 15 I got another letter saying the pay stubs were older than 30 days, which they were by then because the Bank took so long. So I sent new pay stubs. Every time I call I get a different person and nobody can see what the last person did. One man told me the file was in underwriting and another woman the same afternoon told me there was no open application at all. In the meantime we keep getting letters saying we are behind and that the Bank may start foreclosure. My husband is not sleeping. We have three kids and this is the only house they have ever lived in. On August 26 I went to the branch on Route 9 because I thought maybe talking to someone in person would help. I met with a loan officer there and I brought my whole folder. He looked through it for maybe five minutes. Then he told me that with my accent and my kind of last name the underwriters would probably not approve me, and that I should think about selling the house while we still have equity. I was so shocked I did not say anything. I have lived in this country for 22 years and I am a citizen. I do not understand what my last name has to do with whether we can pay our mortgage, which we have done for ten years. I went home and cried. I did not tell my husband what he said for a week because I was ashamed, and I should not have been the one who was ashamed. I want three things. First, I want someone to actually review our modification application, which has been complete since August 15 at the latest. Second, I want the foreclosure letters to stop while the application is being reviewed. Third, I want the Bank to know what that loan officer said to me and to do something about it, because if he said it to me he has said it to other people. I can give the date and time of the meeting and I can describe him. Please do not send me another form letter. I have enough of those to wallpaper my kitchen. Thank you for reading this.
